title: Downloads
summary: The download card: LYGO's own parallel engine, the operator's Plexo install, what is downloading now and what has already landed.

surfaces.usb: DEGRADED(the Plexo half needs the operator to run scripts/fetch_plexo.ps1 on this stick - a 246 MB installer - while LYGO's own engine works with no payload at all and reads the Plexo rows as 'not installed here', which is a true reading, not a fault)
surfaces.web: N/A(by the same steward decision as the other cards that report on local processes: a browser tab has no download engine of its own and no folder to report on)

notes: Read-out (family 'info'), the facts half of the download pair. Every row is asked of its OWNER: plexo_tools.state() for what is installed and what is answering, jobs() for the live jobs (bytes, percent, MB/s, streams), pin() for the pinned upstream release, credit() for who wrote what and under which licence. Nothing is re-derived here, so this card cannot drift out of step with the limb the agent calls. WHAT IT WILL NOT DO: it never claims a download is faster without the job's own numbers; it names the two halves SEPARATELY (LYGO's engine, which ships here, and Plexo, which is a fetched payload) because a kit can have one and not the other; and a kit with no Plexo stays a TRUE reading ('not installed here; run scripts/fetch_plexo.ps1') rather than a red fault. It owns no state, writes nothing and gates nothing - its own test scans this source for write calls.
